title: IPEX Contract API testing approach and recommendation
content:
This page is out of date. For any API contract testing, it is advisable to use the PACT framework approach. It has been tried a couple of times within IPEX, but not yet fully applied anywhere.

Contact for an intro.

What is Contract API testing?

The benefit of Contract API testing specially consumer driven is that you get to test the best of both worlds. You can test using Mocks (quick, cheap, fast to implement) and using real time dependency with an E2E fully deployed environment.

To put it simply — with contract testing, you work with mocks that represent the agreed-upon API contract between the services, but also, the services (producers) that provide the API for consumption have to uphold that API contract that is used in those mocks. The contract is enforced in their CI so they can’t break the API and go to production.

SO a combined approach of both consumer and producer driven API testing is highly recommended , specially in today’s world of complex SOAs, micro-services driven architectures.

Test Strategy:

4 Key players : Consumer, Producer, Contracts and Broker

Role:

Consumer interacts with dependent service through an API provided by the producer. The interaction can be done via another back-end API provided by a different producer or the same producer. Or the interaction can be done by a front-end browser version.

Contract plays a KEY role in defining how the request response model should look like. That means it defines the agreement between the consumer and producer on how the API should behave.

Producer develops and exposes the service. It can maintain its own version of test suits for local testing and mapping for a compliance with the Contract.

Broker holds the contracts and provides added value such as displaying whether contracts have been verified, what interactions exist between services, and other features.
